Rapid growth

The Shale Boom

A shale gas boom is coming to Pittsburgh. The fuel discount will end long before a new gas plant wears out.

Play The Shale Boom↗ Your decisions ↓

Choose your difficulty before you start. It’s free to play in your browser.

Location
Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania
Starts in
2006
Your term
20 years

Your starting point

You begin in 2006 with a coal plant. As your utility grows, a regional gas glut makes a new gas plant an attractive way to meet demand.

During a winter freeze, gas gets more expensive just as gas plants produce less. When the boom ends, the regional discount disappears altogether.

Learn how to play

Your decisions

  1. 01

    Decide how much gas to build

    Compare the fuel savings during the boom with what that same plant will cost you to run afterward.

  2. 02

    Prepare for the freeze

    Check which other plants can pick up the load if your gas units lose output at the same time.

  3. 03

    Make room for new customers

    Use the demand forecast to decide when to build. Keep enough cash to run the fleet you already own.

How much of a twenty-year investment would you bet on cheap gas?
